about: Two grahas sharing one house. AstroBot works from house positions, not degrees, so these are same-house conjunctions rather than close ones; the engine says so in the reading.

rules.says: Sun with Moon: will and feeling pull in the same direction, which gives force but leaves little distance from oneself. Born near a new moon.
Sun with Mars: considerable heat in the temperament, effective in a fight and quick to find one.
Sun with Jupiter: principle and position reinforce each other, and advice is given with authority even when it was not sought.
Sun with Venus: drawn to art, display and refinement; Venus close to the Sun loses some of its ease, so pleasure and duty compete.
Sun with Saturn: authority and restriction in one place. Recognition comes late, the father is a complicated subject, and self-doubt does the work that confidence should.

rules.name: Grahan dosha (solar)
rules.says: Sun with Rahu: ambition outruns position, and the sense of self takes on something borrowed or performed. Classically read as an eclipse of the Sun significations.
Sun with Ketu: detachment from status and from the father; capable, and privately indifferent to being seen as capable.
Moon with Mercury: feeling is put into words quickly and accurately, which suits writing, teaching and negotiation.
Moon with Jupiter: generous by instinct and widely liked; the fullest form of the Gajakesari combination.
Moon with Venus: affectionate, aesthetically alert, and dependent on pleasant surroundings more than is usually admitted.

rules.name: Vish yoga
rules.says: Moon with Saturn: the mind runs cold and heavy. Realistic to a fault, slow to trust, and prone to long low stretches that look like patience from outside.
rules.note: Also called Punarphoo by some authorities, who apply the name specifically to delay in marriage rather than to temperament.

rules.says: Moon with Rahu: imagination amplified past what it can carry; strong intuitions, some of them unreliable, and real difficulty settling the mind.
Moon with Ketu: emotional withdrawal that can look like composure; attachment is felt and then quietly released.
Mars with Mercury: sharp, fast argument and genuine technical skill; the tongue is used as an instrument and occasionally as a weapon.
Mars with Jupiter: conviction backed by the willingness to act on it, which is effective and occasionally righteous.
Mars with Venus: strong appetites and a direct way of pursuing them; artistically forceful, romantically impatient.
Mars with Saturn: drive and restraint locked together. Capable of sustained hard work, and of frustration that accumulates without an outlet.

rules.name: Angarak yoga
rules.says: Mars with Rahu: force without brakes. Decisive and physically bold, with a real risk of acting first and understanding afterwards.
Mars with Ketu: precise, surgical capability; aggression is applied narrowly and then withdrawn.
Mercury with Jupiter: learning becomes doctrine and then gets taught well; the classical signature of a scholar.
Mercury with Venus: persuasive, well-mannered and commercially able; a natural fit for design, trade and diplomacy.
Mercury with Saturn: slow, methodical and unusually accurate thinking. Speech is withheld until it is certain, which is often mistaken for dullness.

rules.name: Guru Chandala yoga
rules.says: Jupiter with Rahu: the teaching function gets mixed with appetite. Unorthodox wisdom, impatience with inherited authority, and a tendency to argue the case for whatever is wanted.
rules.note: Some practitioners read this combination as a positive signature for unconventional learning and treat the classical warning as moralising. Both readings circulate.

rules.says: Jupiter with Ketu: wisdom turned inward; drawn to renunciation and genuinely uninterested in the rewards that Jupiter usually brings.
Jupiter with Saturn: expansion and limit in the same place. Mature judgement, built slowly, with optimism that has been tested rather than assumed.
Venus with Saturn: affection held under discipline. Loyal and undemonstrative, with pleasure postponed often enough to become a habit.
Venus with Rahu: strong and unconventional attractions, often across a boundary of culture, age or circumstance.
Venus with Ketu: desire that arrives and then loses interest in itself; relationships are entered sincerely and held loosely.

rules.name: Shrapit dosha
rules.says: Saturn with Rahu: obstruction with ambition behind it. Long delays, inherited difficulty, and gains that arrive only after the person has stopped expecting them.
rules.note: The name Shrapit is modern and the doctrine is not classical in this form. The underlying judgement about Saturn and Rahu together is.

rules.says: Saturn with Ketu: endurance without attachment to the outcome, which is either austerity or resignation depending on the rest of the chart.
